children: Chicago Mercantile Exchange cattle futures rose for a second consecutive day on Thursday, supported by technical buying as tight cattle supplies overshadowed concerns about beef demand.
Feeder cattle futures climbed and live cattle reached a three-week peak after actively-traded nearby contracts broke through technical chart resistance at key moving averages.

Markets were also underpinned by expectations for continued tight supplies ahead of a USDA report due on Friday. Analysts, on average, believe the report will show on-feed cattle supplies as of November 1 slightly below a year ago, and October placements down 3% from last year.

"We're going to tighten the on-feed supply and, for now at least, futures are trying to suggest that's going to more than offset a little consumer demand concern," said Rich Nelson, chief strategist with Allendale.
The wholesale choice boxed beef cutout value fell $2.44 to $353.52 per hundredweight on Thursday, while select cuts dropped $2.48 to $341.97 per cwt, the USDA said.

CME lean hog futures rose on Thursday, lifted by short covering after two sessions of declines that dragged prices to contract lows a day earlier.
However, weak consumer demand for pork remained a headwind for the market.
December lean hog futures (LHZ26) settled 1.075 cents higher at 52.425 cents per pound. February hogs (LHG27) ended up 0.900 cent at 58.050 cents a pound.
The wholesale pork carcass cutout value fell 82 cents on Thursday to $68.66 per cwt, just above a six-year low of $68.44 on Tuesday, the USDA said.
